label: ordinal numerals to tenth
note: CLOSED by the ordinal tranche, chapters 62-63, one word a lesson, in the order Sanskrit's own construction dictates rather than in numerical order. Chapter 62 opens at FIFTH, because -ma is the ending that generalizes -- it makes 5, 7, 8, 9 and 10 with nothing else changing -- and a rule must be visible before a departure from it is legible. It skips SIX on purpose and says so. Chapter 63 then works OUTWARD from that hole: sasthah is strange until caturthah makes -tha a pair; trtiyah is a third oddity until dvitiyah makes -tiya a pair; and prathamah arrives last because it can only be recognised as a DIFFERENT KIND of word once nine words of the same kind have gone past -- Macdonell records it as pra-tama, a superlative of pra 'forward', with no numeral in it at all. The grouping is read off the dictionary rather than asserted: Macdonell prints the join inside every one of the ten headwords, and the chapter-63 payoff prints that table with his page numbers. CORRECTION TO THIS NOTE'S OWN PREVIOUS TEXT: it claimed the missing ordinals were also why SA-A1-SP-02 was uncovered. That was wrong. SP-02 is RELATIVE POSITION -- left, right, above, below, in front, behind -- and it is uncovered because vamam, daksinam, upari, adhah, agre and pascat are taught nowhere. Closing the ordinals does not touch it. NOT CLAIMED HERE: ordinals above tenth, and the feminine forms in -i that Macdonell lists for several of these -- no lesson teaches a feminine ordinal and none is probed.
